proof_audit.topic: Sharp cutoff target and continuous versions
proof_audit.independent_review: On either side the treatment rule and consistency equate the observed conditional mean to the corresponding potential-outcome mean almost everywhere. The one-sided limits equal the values at zero of the maintained continuous versions. If two continuous versions differed at a supported point, they would differ on a neighborhood having positive probability, contradicting almost-everywhere equality. Hence the cutoff target is well defined despite P(R=0)=0. Equality of an arbitrary conditional expectation value on a null event would not suffice.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: Continuous potential-outcome mean versions on a neighborhood and positive score density on both sides; consistency and the sharp rule. The result is local, not a finite-window randomization or external-validity statement.

proof_audit.independent_review: For the quadratic sharp model, exact uniform window integration gives right mean 5+h+h²/3 and left mean 2−h/2+h²/3, so the contrast is 3+3h/2. Setting both potential outcomes equal to the observed piecewise curve leaves (R,D,Y) unchanged with zero individual effects, violating continuity. In the independent U/V sorting construction, conditioning on U fixes the sign and |V| is uniform. Each half line has density 1/2 while Y(0)=Y(1)=U jumps in composition at zero. Smooth density therefore does not prove the required outcome continuity.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: The counterexamples distinguish one observed distribution from causal completions and distinguish an outcome discontinuity from a density discontinuity. They do not claim that a particular observed dataset has been validated.

proof_audit.topic: Local linear weights and same-data correction
proof_audit.independent_review: Independently used centered regression: w_j=K_j/ΣK−xbar K_j(x_j−xbar)/ΣK(x−xbar)². This reproduces constants and a zero linear moment. Lagrange interpolation yields quadratic cutoff weights without using the author normal-equation inverse. The positive distances 1/10,1/5,3/10 give w=(4/3,1/3,−2/3), v=(3,−3,1), and leading-coefficient weights q=(50,−100,50). Adding q/30 to w yields v. Equal independent noise gives old jump variance 14σ²/3, added-correction variance 100σ²/3, covariance zero, corrected variance 38σ². A peer transfer with variance multipliers (1,2,1) instead gives covariance −20σ²/9 and corrected variance 56σ², confirming zero covariance is design specific.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: Fixed nonzero scores on one side, nonnegative effective kernels, identified slope; correction estimates use the same observations. The finite variance statement assumes the stipulated known independent Gaussian noise, not an estimated variance or adaptive bandwidth.

proof_audit.independent_review: Taylor expansion with bounded second derivatives gives each intercept bias at most (L_s/2)Σ|w_j|r_j², since constant and linear reproduction hold. The computed unsigned moment is 13/150, so L+=10 and L−=2 give B=13/25. If |bias|≤B, the event |noise|≤z_(.975) SE implies |estimate−target|≤B+z SE. Thus the interval has at least 95% coverage under the known Gaussian law. Decimal integration independently gives radius 0.9434006120674119. The corrected unbiased estimator with the old SE has coverage 2Φ(z sqrt((14/3)/38))−1=0.5078205300463541. This is not a uniform claim about all bias correction.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: Predetermined scores and widths, known noise variance and the stated deterministic derivative bounds; B is a triangle bound, not asserted sharp. The event argument covers every admitted mean bias, separately from the finite endpoint numerical check.

proof_audit.topic: Arbitrary-k identities, scaling and rate undersmoothing
proof_audit.independent_review: Substituting the elementary sums of j, j² and j³ into the centered-regression expression gives w_j=2(2k+1−3j)/(k(k−1)), Σw=1, Σjw=0, Σj²w=−(k+1)(k+2)/6 and Σw²=2(2k+1)/(k(k−1)). Hence b=−δq(k+1)(k+2)/(6n²), V=4σ²(2k+1)/(k(k−1)). With k≈nh, leading MSE is δq²h⁴/36+8σ²/(nh); differentiation gives h_opt⁵=72σ²/(δq²n), and at this optimum squared bias/variance tends to 1/4. Since nh_opt grows as n^(4/5), floor rounding has vanishing relative error. A fixed fraction r leaves |b|/SE→r^(5/2)/2. For h=n^(−a), 1/5<a<1 is the sufficient rate condition; a=1/4 works. Cauchy-Schwarz yields Σ|w|≤sqrt(10) and V≤20σ²/k, giving the stated deterministic-curvature consistency bound.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: n denotes observations available per side; 2≤k≤n. Nonzero curvature contrast for the interior leading optimum, fixed independent Gaussian errors for exact coverage, and no data-selected bandwidth. The formulas and finite illustrations do not establish a generic nonparametric RBC theorem.

proof_audit.topic: Fuzzy type population and signed decomposition
proof_audit.independent_review: With a common cutoff distribution of compliance types, each type mean has the same limiting untreated and treated values from the two sides. Exclusion removes direct eligibility effects. Always and never takers cancel from the limit difference; under monotonicity only compliers remain, giving ΔY=P(C)E[effect|C] and ΔD=P(C)>0. The original masses give limits D=(1/4,3/4), Y=(5/2,9/2), LATE 4 and ATE 7/2. A direct eligibility increment 1/2 makes the ratio 5 while preserving the first stage. Under the separate defier model, ΔY=(3/8)4−(1/8)8=1/2 and ΔD=1/4, so ratio 2 is a signed type contrast.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: Constant type proportions near the cutoff, continuous type-conditional potential means, consistency, no spillovers and the explicitly imposed exclusion/monotonicity conditions. Positive first stage alone neither establishes them nor identifies the population ATE.

proof_audit.topic: Simplex existence, fitted-predictor uniqueness and ties
proof_audit.independent_review: The finite simplex is compact and nonempty; continuous quadratic loss attains a minimum. Distinct fitted predictors at two minima would make their feasible midpoint improve loss by one quarter of the squared positive-definite V norm of their fit difference. Thus the fitted predictor is unique, while weights are unique exactly when no other feasible weight has the same fit, equivalently no nonzero zero-sum feasible flat direction at the optimum. Full column rank of the augmented donor matrix is sufficient but not necessary. Sequentially minimizing weight coordinates over compact nested minimizer sets defines the lexicographic tie rule.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: V is predetermined and positive definite; nonnegative weights may equal zero. A tie rule resolves an algorithm, not a causal identification problem. The peer geometric solver checks Euclidean two-dimensional cases, while the general V-norm statement was audited analytically.

proof_audit.independent_review: With untreated training outcome vectors, common noiseless factors imply e=F_pre Δλ. Full column rank yields a left inverse L and Δλ=Le; exact fit then gives exact future counterfactuals. With nonzero e, future discrepancy is f_t′Le and is bounded by ||f_t′L|| ||e||. Full rank is not necessary for a particular future date: if f_t is in the row span of F_pre, every unobserved loading in ker(F_pre) is annihilated. A peer transfer with pre rows (1,0),(2,0) and loading difference (0,7) verifies zero discrepancy for future (3,0) and discrepancy 7 for (0,1).
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: No anticipation, unaffected donors, noiseless shared untreated factor model, training on outcomes rather than arbitrary predictors, and the declared rank or future-row-space condition. No stochastic-error or unknown-factor estimation theorem is inherited.

proof_audit.independent_review: Adding a factor that is zero in every preperiod and (1,2) post-treatment, with treated loading one and donor loadings zero, preserves all observed data while changing the treated untreated path and compensating effects. The pre-factor matrix has a zero column. Separately increasing observed donor B post outcomes by 2 changes the data and the forecast by one; it is a spillover sensitivity case, not observational equivalence. With duplicate donor preperiods and post values 2,8, all weights fit; prediction 8−6w spans [2,8] and effect −1+6w spans [−1,5]. Each point is attainable under a maintained fixed donor-mixture law, establishing sharpness only within that law. An unconstrained post-only factor can escape the range.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: The observed panel held fixed in the first construction is distinguished from changed donor observations in the second. Good prefit, holdout fit and an optimizer range do not by themselves identify a causal effect.

proof_audit.topic: Fully replayed placebo ranks under the actual law
proof_audit.independent_review: Under a sharp null, fix the complete outcome panel and rerun the same prespecified algorithm for every candidate label. Group tied scores and order groups from largest down. The inclusive upper-tail value at each group is cumulative actual assignment mass. Rejection at p≤α is either empty or a full upper tail whose mass equals its lowest included p and is ≤α. This works with nonuniform known masses and the explicit +infinity top category for zero-pre/positive-post error; zero/zero is score zero. The independent convex-hull refits recover all four square-panel forecasts (1,1), losses 2, gaps 7/2,−3,−2,3/2, and both sets of tails.
proof_audit.scope_and_conditions: The actual assignment law and sharp null calibrate ranks. Uniform observational ranks are benchmark comparisons unless uniform assignment is defended. Full procedure replay includes fitting/tie/donor rules; a correct factor forecast is not required for the finite rank proof.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Prove sharp continuity identification, explain the zero-probability cutoff and construct same observations without identification.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: One-sided observed means recover continuous potential-outcome versions; positive support makes the version unique. P(R=0)=0 prevents an arbitrary conditional value from being the target. Setting both potentials to the observed piecewise curve yields exactly the same observations and zero effects while violating continuity.
prompt_solution_audit.answer_and_method_check: Compared with the complete printed solution and the methods taught before the prompt; no material discrepancy.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Compute wide/narrow means and analyze density-preserving sorting, then distinguish local randomization.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Exact quadratic integration gives 3+3h/2, hence 9/2 at h=1 and 33/10 at h=1/5. In the sorting construction each side has density 1/2 and all treatment effects are zero, but the observed outcome jumps from 0 to 1. A randomized finite window additionally needs its own assignment and score-exclusion restrictions.

Linear jump mean is 28/15 rather than target 2; quadratic jump mean is 2. Variances are 14σ²/3 and 38σ². Negative outcome weights perform local extrapolation; they are not treatment probabilities.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Calculate estimated-correction variance and covariance, old-SE coverage and a curvature-aware interval.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Leading quadratic coefficient weights are 50(1,−2,1). Added correction q/30 has jump variance 100σ²/3 and zero covariance with the original jump in this specific design. Corrected variance is 38σ², giving old-SE coverage 0.5078205300463541. Unsigned moment 13/150 with curvature bounds 10 and 2 gives B=13/25 and radius 0.9434006120674119. The triangle event proves at least 95% coverage under the specified Gaussian contract.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Establish arbitrary-grid formulas, derive optimal width and analyze fixed fractions and proper undersmoothing.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Direct sum identities produce exact b=−δq(k+1)(k+2)/(6n²) and V=4σ²(2k+1)/(k(k−1)). Differentiate leading MSE to obtain h_opt⁵=72σ²/(δq²n); scaled bias tends to 1/2, so nominal normal coverage tends to 0.9209024658394033. A fixed fraction r leaves r^(5/2)/2; h=n^(−1/4) makes scaled bias vanish while local information grows. Cauchy-Schwarz gives sqrt(10) absolute-weight and 20σ²/k variance bounds. Integer rounding is negligible relative to nh_opt→infinity.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Compute all cutoff type limits and estimands, add direct eligibility, then introduce defiers.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Original D limits are 1/4 and 3/4, Y limits 5/2 and 9/2; the local ratio 4 differs from ATE 7/2. Adding eligibility/2 gives Y contrast 5/2 and ratio 5: exclusion fails. The defier table gives D limits 3/8 and 5/8, Y limits 7/2 and 4, ratio 2. This lies outside the complier/defier effect interval [4,8] because monotonicity fails and weights are signed. Common-cutoff type conditions, not merely a positive first stage, justify the decomposition.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Construct a same-observed hidden-factor alternative and contrast a changed-data donor-spillover case.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: The hidden factor is zero in every preperiod and (1,2) in the two postperiods, with only the treated loading nonzero. prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Solve the degenerate donor fit and delimit the sharpness claim.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Every (w,1−w) is optimal. Prediction 8−6w spans [2,8]; gap −1+6w spans [−1,5]. Lexicographic minimization chooses (0,1), prediction 8 and gap −1. Each mixture constructs a full compatible untreated path and effect under the maintained fixed-mixture restriction; absent that restriction a post-only treated factor puts the counterfactual outside this range.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Refit all placebo candidates, compare actual and uniform label laws, and prove inclusive rank validity with boundary scores.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Each geometric projection fits (1,1) with pre-MSE 1. Signed gaps are (7/2,−3,−2,3/2); ratios are their absolute values. Uniform tails are (1/4,1/2,3/4,1); at α=1/4 size is 1/4 and at 5% size is zero. For actual masses (7/10,1/10,1/10,1/10), the false uniform test has size 7/10. Actual tails (7/10,4/5,9/10,1) reject with probability zero at 1/4. Ordered whole tied tails prove the general finite result, including +infinity and zero/zero categories.

prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt_scope: Evaluate the research report using the exact six-objection, two-repair and conclusion rubric.
prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Six distinct objections concern fixed-fraction undersmoothing, density nonrejection, neglected correction uncertainty, post-selected donors, unsupported perfect-prefit extrapolation and falsely randomized observational ranks. Each earns one point. Two repairs, worth two points each, must separately state an RD target/continuity/inference contract and a prespecified donor/training/holdout protocol plus remaining limitations. The two-point conclusion separates counterfactual assumptions, estimation and calibration. Total 12; no required effect sign or estimator brand.

independent_numerical_method.gaussian_accuracy: The normal integral uses an alternating integrated exponential series at |x|≤8 with 50-digit Decimal arithmetic; beyond k=32 the absolute terms decrease. Stopping below 1e−43 bounds the remaining alternating tail before float conversion. The 2e−12 comparison tolerance safely exceeds float rounding and the precision of the printed 12-decimal anchors. The quantile uses 56 bisections on [0,3].
independent_numerical_method.bounded_scope: Local fits have 2–32 scores; geometric problems have two coordinates and two or three donors; types have 2–4 rows; label laws have 2–8 positive masses; exact input magnitudes ≤10^6; closed-form grid counts satisfy 2≤k≤n≤10^8. No undirected grid search or empirical data claim.
independent_numerical_method.numeric_vs_literal_anchors: The 70 solution anchors include computed exact/rounded values and a small set of required assumption/rubric words; they are not represented as 70 distinct numerical calculations.
